results.content:
Title: Review: Code review on your own machine, with optional AI | Product Hunt
# Review. ## Code review on your own machine, with optional AI. A desktop app for Git branches and GitHub pull requests. Comment on any line, publish when you're ready, and add an AI reviewer with your own model, or none. Launch tags:Open Source•Developer Tools•Artificial Intelligence. I'm Hamed, and I made Review. I'm a developer and team lead. Since AI started writing so much of our code, reviewing it all has become the hardest part of my job. So I built Review: a desktop app for reviewing pull requests, where you can set up a team of AI reviewers from different providers to take the first pass. You still decide what gets published. - Opens your local Git branches and GitHub pull requests in one window. ⌘P jumps to any of them. - Pins each review to exact commits, so the diff doesn't shift when someone pushes. - Keeps your comments on your machine until you publish them to GitHub as a review. - Adds an AI reviewer if you want one: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, or a local model in Ollama or LM Studio. Your keys are stored in the system keychain. **What's different about the AI part**: it checks every change against a fixed set of rules (bugs, security, error handling, tests and more), and it shows which rules it actually checked, not just what it found. If a request fails, you can retry only the rules it missed. It can also call your MCP servers for context the code doesn't have, like the ticket behind a change. It's free, open source (MIT) and needs no account. It runs on macOS, Windows and Linux. One heads-up: the installers aren't signed yet, so your system will ask once the first time you open it. The website has the two-click fix. I'd love to know: what's the most annoying part of code review for you today? And which model would you plug in first? Title: Best UX for leaving a product review? : Product Hunt Discussion Forums | Product Hunt
### Topic Forums. ### Product Forums. # Best UX for leaving a product review? We're re-thinking our leave-a-review flow (you all are leaving lots of reviews, including founder reviews!) and I wonder if anyone has review flows they think are 1) easy to use, and 2) actually help you write better reviews. I'm looking at G2, Trustpilot, Yelp, Google...nothing's standing out as amazing. Would love any UX inspiration here! ### Replies. love that you are asking your users about this :). If I were to redesign the flow, I’d probably take inspiration and ideas from the following:. **Airbnb’s friendly tone:** They excel at emotional prompting and building a social connection with the host, in your case, the Maker. For example they use: “Tell your host what you loved.”. **Typeform’s single-question rhythm:** A guided, progressive flow instead of one big blank box. You could even break it into one card or screen per question, which is psychologically easier to complete than a long form. **Notion’s micro-prompting:** They break prompts into tiny, targeted cues, what I called micro-prompts. For example, in their template gallery feedback flow, you might see:. “What problem did this template solve for you?”. “What’s your favorite part of using it?”. “Anything you’d like to improve?”. These prompts appear inside the text area as placeholder text, disappearing as soon as the user starts typing. Finally, once the new user feedback flow is designed (but before development), I’d run a quick user test to make sure it works well and to see how users respond. For that, you could use our platform Uxia, which lets you run user testing in under 5 minutes thanks to AI. We’re launching on the 23rd, and I’d be happy to walk you through a product demo or onboard anyone from your team :). @borja\_diazroig where are you seeing Notion's "micro-prompting"? Do you have a screenshot or URL? I'm not familiar with it, but I'm intrigued! Yeah would love to see a product demo! Comment on any line, publish when you're ready, and add an AI reviewer with your own model, or none. ## Products used by Review. ### Explore the tech stack and tools that power Review. See what products Review uses for development, design, marketing, analytics, and more. Electron FiddleCreate, run, package, and share experiments with Electron. Electron let me ship Review as a real desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux from one codebase, with access to Git, the file system and the system keychain. OllamaThe easiest way to run large language models locally. Ollama is how Review offers fully local AI code review. Pick a model, and your code never leaves your machine. Its OpenAI-compatible API made the integration straightforward. Claude by AnthropicA family of foundational AI models. Built much of Review with Claude Code: from the AI review runner to the retry and stop/resume flow. It handled the whole loop, from code and tests to PRs and the release, and kept the codebase consistent as it grew.
